title: Vertical Angles and Angles Formed by Parallel Lines
seo_title: Geometry Angles and Parallel Lines Worksheets (TEKS G.6A)
standard_text: G.6A verify theorems about angles formed by the intersection of lines and line segments, including vertical angles, and angles formed by parallel lines cut by a transversal and prove equidistance between the endpoints of a segment and points on its perpendicular bisector and apply these relationships to solve problems; G.5A investigate patterns to make conjectures about geometric relationships, including angles formed by parallel lines cut by a transversal
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.6A and G.5A: vertical angles, linear pairs, angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal, solving for x and proving lines parallel. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Parallel lines: congruent pairs, or supplementary same-side angles.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Vertical angles are congruent. A linear pair adds to 180°.
  • With parallel lines: corresponding, alternate interior and alternate exterior angles are congruent.
  • Same-side (consecutive) interior angles are supplementary.
  • If these angle facts are true, the lines are parallel (the converses).

Examples

Example

Alternate interior angles: (3x + 10)° and (5x − 30)°

3x + 10 = 5x − 30

Answer: x = 20

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding to 90° instead of 180°A linear pair makes a straight line.
Calling same-side interior angles congruentThey are supplementary.
Using the converse backwardsAngle facts prove the lines parallel.

items.q: Which fact is enough to prove ℓ ∥ m?
items.e: If same-side interior angles are supplementary, the lines are parallel. Vertical angles and linear pairs are always true, so they prove nothing. m∠3 + m∠5 = 180°

items.e: The angles are alternate exterior angles and they are congruent (118°), so ℓ ∥ m. Yes.

items.q: Line t is perpendicular to line ℓ, and line ℓ is parallel to line m. What angle does t make with m?
items.e: Corresponding angles are congruent. t makes 90° with ℓ, so it also makes 90° with m.

items.q: Lines ℓ and m are parallel. Find x.
items.e: Draw a line through the bend, parallel to ℓ and m. It splits x into two parts that are alternate interior angles with 41° and 35°. So x = 41 + 35 = 76.

items.q: A road crosses two parallel railroad tracks. One angle between the road and the first track is 59°. What is the same-side interior angle at the second track?
items.e: Same-side interior angles with parallel lines are supplementary: 180° − 59° = 121°.

items.q: Oak Street and Pine Street are parallel. Main Street crosses both. The angle on the north side of Oak Street, east of Main Street, is 51°. What is the corresponding angle at Pine Street?
items.e: Corresponding angles formed by parallel streets are congruent: 51°.

items.q: Oak Street and Pine Street are parallel. Main Street crosses both. The angle on the north side of Oak Street, east of Main Street, is 56°. What is the corresponding angle at Pine Street?

items.q: A road crosses two parallel railroad tracks. One angle between the road and the first track is 46°. What is the same-side interior angle at the second track?

items.q: The handrail of a staircase is parallel to the line of the stairs. The stairs make a 39° angle with the floor. The handrail post is vertical. What acute angle does the handrail make with the post?
items.e: The handrail makes a 39° angle with the horizontal (corresponding angles). The post is vertical, at 90° to the horizontal, so the angle between the rail and the post is 90° − 39° = 51°.

items.q: The handrail of a staircase is parallel to the line of the stairs. The stairs make a 35° angle with the floor. The handrail post is vertical. What acute angle does the handrail make with the post?
items.e: The handrail makes a 35° angle with the horizontal (corresponding angles). The post is vertical, at 90° to the horizontal, so the angle between the rail and the post is 90° − 35° = 55°.

items.q: Lines ℓ and m are parallel. Find x.
items.e: Draw a line through the bend, parallel to ℓ and m. It splits x into two parts that are alternate interior angles with 30° and 35°. So x = 30 + 35 = 65.
